parts.name: FuriosaAI RNGD PCIe accelerator, 48GB HBM3
parts.host_requirements: server/workstation with PCIe Gen5 x16, 12VHPWR power and passive-card airflow
parts.software_stack: Furiosa SDK / Furiosa-LLM / OpenAI-compatible server / native PyTorch integration
parts.plain_language: RNGD is a current purpose-built LLM inference card rather than a generic TOPS-only NPU. It combines 48GB HBM3 with a production Furiosa-LLM stack and an OpenAI-compatible serving path, making it one of the strongest non-GPU accelerator references in the catalog.
parts.source_notes: FuriosaAI documents 48GB HBM3, 1.5TB/s memory bandwidth, PCIe Gen5 x16 and 180W TDP. Current 2026 documentation includes Furiosa-LLM, an OpenAI-compatible server and supported LLM deployment; Furiosa states RNGD is in mass production. No public single-card acquisition price is asserted.

parts.name: Tenstorrent Blackhole p150, 32GB GDDR6
parts.host_requirements: PCIe Gen5 x16 workstation/server, ATX 3.1-class PSU, 12V-2x6 power and cooling appropriate to p150 variant
parts.software_stack: TT-Metalium / TT-NN / TT-Forge / tt-inference-server / vLLM Tenstorrent integration
parts.plain_language: Blackhole p150 is a current open-stack AI ASIC with 32GB of local GDDR6 and an actively released LLM inference server. It is power-hungry compared with edge NPUs, but it is valuable as a purchasable non-GPU reference with real Llama/Falcon model support rather than a marketing-only accelerator.
parts.source_notes: Tenstorrent documents p150 with 32GB GDDR6, 512GB/s bandwidth, PCIe 5.0 x16 and 300W TBP. Tenstorrent's 2026 tt-inference-server releases explicitly exercise Llama 3.1 8B and Falcon3 7B on p150. The $1,399 figure is Tenstorrent's published p150 reference price; live checkout availability can change.

parts.name: Tenstorrent Wormhole n300s, 24GB GDDR6
parts.host_requirements: PCIe Gen4 x16 host, EPS12V power and server-style airflow for passive n300s
parts.software_stack: TT-Metalium / TT-NN / TT-Forge / tt-inference-server / vLLM Tenstorrent integration
parts.plain_language: n300s doubles the Wormhole silicon and memory of n150 into one 24GB card. Tenstorrent continues to ship and support the Wormhole inference stack, so this is a useful current/used-market bridge between small accelerator cards and newer Blackhole hardware.
parts.source_notes: Tenstorrent lists n300s at $1,399 and documents 24GB GDDR6, 576GB/s bandwidth, PCIe 4.0 x16 and 300W board power. Tenstorrent's inference-server releases include Llama and other transformer models on Wormhole devices and multi-device Wormhole systems.

parts.name: AMD Alveo U250 64GB DDR4 secondary-market watch
parts.host_requirements: PCIe Gen3 x16 host, 8-pin auxiliary power, server/workstation cooling, XRT/Vitis deployment environment
parts.software_stack: AMD XRT / Vitis / Vivado; custom RTL/HLS/OpenCL; legacy machine-learning flows
parts.plain_language: U250 is interesting because 64GB of card-attached DDR4 can appear cheaply as datacenter FPGA hardware ages out. AMD still publishes current XRT/Vitis packages, but there is no project-approved plug-and-play LLM runtime: treat it as a programmable research target, not a 64GB GPU substitute.
parts.source_notes: AMD documents 64GB DDR4 ECC, 77GB/s bandwidth, PCIe Gen3 x16 and 215W electrical design power. AMD says U250 remains supported for current users while recommending V80 for new designs; current Ubuntu 24.04 XRT/deployment packages are published. Used price must be sourced separately.

parts.name: AMD Alveo U200 64GB DDR4 secondary-market watch
parts.host_requirements: PCIe Gen3 x16 host, auxiliary power, server/workstation cooling, XRT/Vitis deployment environment
parts.software_stack: AMD XRT / Vitis / Vivado; custom RTL/HLS/OpenCL; legacy machine-learning flows
parts.plain_language: U200 is the smaller-fabric sibling to U250 but keeps the same 64GB DDR4 capacity. It belongs on the secondary-market watch because AMD still ships a current software runtime for existing users, while any transformer acceleration would require substantial custom FPGA work.
parts.source_notes: AMD documents U200 with 64GB DDR4 and actively supported current-user XRT/Vitis packages while steering new designs to V80. The card is a large-memory programmable accelerator watch, not a proven local-LLM card, and used acquisition price remains unresolved.
